sections.heading: Writing and recording
sections.wikitext:
[[Barry Gibb|Barry]] and [[Robin Gibb]] wrote the song in August 1970 with "[[Lonely Days]]" when the Gibb brothers had reconvened following a period of break-up and alienation. "Robin came to my place," says Barry, "and that afternoon we wrote 'How Can You Mend a Broken Heart' and that obviously was a link to us coming back together." They originally offered the song to [[Andy Williams]], but ended up recording it themselves, although Williams did later cover the song on his album ''You've Got a Friend''.<ref name="recording">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KugbDQHX0R8C&q=how+can+you+mend+a+broken+heart+bee+gees&pg=PT627 |title=The Bee Gees - Tales of the Brothers Gibb |last=Hughes |first=Andrew |year=2009 |publisher=Omnibus Press |isbn=9780857120045 |access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref> 

The single version was recorded on 28 January 1971 in [[London]].<ref name="credited">{{cite web|url=http://www.columbia.edu/~brennan/beegees/71.html |title=Gibb Songs: 1971 |last=Brennan |first=Joseph |access-date=13 January 2014}}</ref> The group's later song "[[My World (Bee Gees song)|My World]]" followed along the same musical ideas on this song.<ref name="recording"/> Robin Gibb's remarked on the song, "The whole thing took about an hour to complete. The song reached the number one spot, to our great satisfaction."<ref name="allmusic">{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/song/how-can-you-mend-a-broken-heart-mt0013424192 |title=Bee Gees - How Can You Mend a Broken Heart |last=Janovitz |first=Bill |website=[[AllMusic]] |publisher=[[Rovi Corporation]] |access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref>
sections.text:
Barry and Robin Gibb wrote the song in August 1970 with "Lonely Days" when the Gibb brothers had reconvened following a period of break-up and alienation. "Robin came to my place," says Barry, "and that afternoon we wrote 'How Can You Mend a Broken Heart' and that obviously was a link to us coming back together." They originally offered the song to Andy Williams, but ended up recording it themselves, although Williams did later cover the song on his album You've Got a Friend. 

The single version was recorded on 28 January 1971 in London. The group's later song "My World" followed along the same musical ideas on this song. Robin Gibb's remarked on the song, "The whole thing took about an hour to complete. The song reached the number one spot, to our great satisfaction."

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
Although failing to chart on the [[UK Singles Chart]], the song became the Bee Gees' first US number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and also reached number four on the ''Billboard'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] chart. ''Billboard'' ranked it as [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1971|the No. 5 song for 1971]].  ''[[Cash Box]]'' described the song as being "a slower, almost country-ballad styled performance which links an intricate melody segment with more powerful thrusts to give the track top forty impetus."<ref>{{cite news|title=CashBox Record Reviews|date=12 June 1971|page=16|access-date=2021-12-10|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1971/Cash-Box-1971-06-12.pdf|newspaper=Cash Box}}</ref> ''[[Record World]]'' called it a "lovely tune [that] can't miss."<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Picks of the Week|magazine=Record World|date=12 June 1971|page=1|access-date=2023-04-22|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/71/RW-1971-06-12.pdf}}</ref> 

Following the release of "How Can You Mend a Broken Heart", the song was nominated for a [[Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Duo Or Group]] along with [[George Harrison]]'s "[[My Sweet Lord]]" and others.<ref name="recording"/> It was performed as part of a medley on ''[[The Midnight Special (TV series)|The Midnight Special]]'' on 10 October 1975, in Japan on the Japanese TV special ''Love Sounds'', and on the ''[[Mr. Natural (Bee Gees album)|Mr. Natural]]'' tour in 1974. A live version recorded on 17 and 18 November 1989, at the [[Melbourne Park|National Tennis Centre]], [[Melbourne, Australia]], was used for the benefit album ''[[Nobody's Child: Romanian Angel Appeal]]''. Between 1997 and 1999, the song was performed on the ''One Night Only'' tour as part of a medley. It was last performed by the Bee Gees in 2001.

Barry Gibb re-recorded the song as a duet with [[Sheryl Crow]] for his 2020 solo album, ''[[Greenfields (album)|Greenfields: The Gibb Brothers Songbook, Vol. 1]].''
sections.text:
Although failing to chart on the UK Singles Chart, the song became the Bee Gees' first US number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and also reached number four on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart. Billboard ranked it as the No. 5 song for 1971.  Cash Box described the song as being "a slower, almost country-ballad styled performance which links an intricate melody segment with more powerful thrusts to give the track top forty impetus." Record World called it a "lovely tune [that] can't miss." 

Following the release of "How Can You Mend a Broken Heart", the song was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Performance by a Duo Or Group along with George Harrison's "My Sweet Lord" and others. It was performed as part of a medley on The Midnight Special on 10 October 1975, in Japan on the Japanese TV special Love Sounds, and on the Mr. Natural tour in 1974. A live version recorded on 17 and 18 November 1989, at the National Tennis Centre, Melbourne, Australia, was used for the benefit album Nobody's Child: Romanian Angel Appeal. Between 1997 and 1999, the song was performed on the One Night Only tour as part of a medley. It was last performed by the Bee Gees in 2001.

Barry Gibb re-recorded the song as a duet with Sheryl Crow for his 2020 solo album, Greenfields: The Gibb Brothers Songbook, Vol. 1.

Al Green version
Other versions
sections.wikitext:
;1970s
*1971: [[Johnny Mathis]] recorded a version of this song for his LP ''[[You've Got a Friend (Johnny Mathis album)|You've Got a Friend]]''.
*1972: [[Al Green]] recorded the song for his album ''[[Let's Stay Together (Al Green album)|Let's Stay Together]]''<ref>{{YouTube|PTY6Kv0nPr8|Al Green - How Can You Mend a Broken Heart (Official Audio)}}</ref> and the song also appeared on the soundtracks of 1997's ''[[Good Will Hunting]]'', 1999's ''[[The Virgin Suicides (film)|The Virgin Suicides]]'', 1999's ''[[Notting Hill (film)|Notting Hill]]'' and 2010's ''[[The Book of Eli]]''. Green's cover was also featured in season 4 episode 2 of the American television series ''[[Atlanta (TV series)|Atlanta]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/atlanta-songs-season-4-music/|title='Atlanta': All the Songs Heard in Season 4|last=Lee|first=Cydney|publisher=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=11 November 2022|access-date=8 February 2025}}</ref> Green's version was released as a single in France on [[Cream Records]]. In 2008, Green's version was remade into a duet with [[Joss Stone]] for the [[Sex and the City: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack|soundtrack]] to the film adaptation of ''[[Sex and the City (film)|Sex and the City]]'', with her vocals [[overdubbing|overdubbed]] onto the track.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.demonmusicgroup.co.uk/NewsArticles.aspx#News10620 |title=Al Green on Sex and the City |access-date=7 July 2008 |date=14 May 2008 |work=[[Demon Music Group]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080712004216/http://www.demonmusicgroup.co.uk/NewsArticles.aspx#News10620 |archive-date=12 July 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hWtKm5WbE_w  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/hWtKm5WbE_w |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Joss Stone - Al Green - How Can You Mend A BrokenHeart |date=27 June 2010 |publisher=[[YouTube]] |access-date=26 January 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref> 
*1973: [[Cher]] covered the song on her 1973 album ''[[Half-Breed (album)|Half-Breed]]''.
*1975: [[Peter Yarrow]] covered the song on his 1975 album ''Love Songs''.
*1977: [[Florence Henderson]] performed the song during a medley on an episode of ''[[The Brady Bunch Hour|The Brady Bunch Variety Hour]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0531059/soundtrack |title=The Brady Bunch Variety Hour - Soundtrack |website=IMDb.com |access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref>
;1980s
*1982: Single released by [[Freddie McGregor]] on Music Lab, produced by [[Coxsone Dodd]].
*1984: Single release by Deirdre and [[Louise Rutkowski]] (later of 4AD supergroup [[This Mortal Coil]]) for their debut "In An Ideal World" (1984) with their first band Sunset Gun.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sunsetgundiscography.yolasite.com/how-do-you-mend-a-broken-heart.php |title=Sunset Gun Discography at YolaSite.com |website=YolaSite.com |access-date=7 October 2021}}</ref>
*1985: Mexican Group ''El Tiempo'' recorded a [[Spanish-language]] version called "Cómo curar un corazón" on their album ''Cada día más''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/cada-dia-mas-mw0000912773|title=El Tiempo - Cada Dia Mas|website=AllMusic.com |access-date=19 June 2023}}</ref>
;1990s
*1991: [[Teddy Pendergrass]] recorded a version of this song on his LP ''[[Truly Blessed]]''.
;2000s
*2003: [[Michael Bublé]] recorded this song, with Barry Gibb performing [[backing vocalist|backup vocals]], on his ''[[Michael Bublé (album)|self-titled album]]''. Bublé's version reached number 22 on the US ''Billboard'' Adult Contemporary chart. It was Buble's first single.
*2003: [[American Idol]]'s second winner [[Ruben Studdard]] covered the song on his debut album ''[[Soulful (Ruben Studdard album)|Soulful]]''.
*2005: [[Mari Wilson]], English pop and jazz singer, included a cover on her album ''Dolled Up''.   
*2005: [[Steve Brookstein]] recorded it on his number-one album ''[[Heart and Soul (Steve Brookstein album)|Heart and Soul]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/music/4549471.stm |title=Entertainment | Album success for X Factor winner |work=BBC News |date=2005-05-15 |access-date=2014-04-12}}</ref>
*2006: The song is covered in [[Julio Iglesias]]'s album ''[[Romantic Classics]]''.
*2007: [[Barry Manilow]]'s version appears on his album ''[[The Greatest Songs of the Seventies]]''.<ref>[http://sev.prnewswire.com/entertainment/20070710/NYTU11510072007-1.html "New Barry Manilow Album, The Greatest Songs of the Seventies, Arrives in Stores September 18th on Arista Records"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926221650/http://sev.prnewswire.com/entertainment/20070710/NYTU11510072007-1.html |date=26 September 2007 }}, PRNewswire, 10 July 2007.</ref>
*2009: [[Jazz]] singer-pianist [[Diana Krall]] covered this song on her album ''[[Quiet Nights (Diana Krall album)|Quiet Nights]]''.
*2009: [[Rod Stewart]] recorded a version for his album ''[[Soulbook]]'', though it was left off the final track listing.
;2010s
*2014: [[Eef Barzelay]] recorded a version for a fundraising CD titled ''More Super Hits of the Seventies'' for freeform radio station [[WFMU]].
*2017: [[Chris Stills]] recorded a version for the feature film ''[[I, Tonya]]''.
*2020: [[Kahil El'Zabar]] recorded an instrumental version titled "How Can We Mend Broken Heart" for his 2020 album ''America the Beautiful''.

*2009: Jazz singer-pianist Diana Krall covered this song on her album Quiet Nights.
*2009: Rod Stewart recorded a version for his album Soulbook, though it was left off the final track listing.
;2010s
*2014: Eef Barzelay recorded a version for a fundraising CD titled More Super Hits of the Seventies for freeform radio station WFMU.
*2017: Chris Stills recorded a version for the feature film I, Tonya.
*2020: Kahil El'Zabar recorded an instrumental version titled "How Can We Mend Broken Heart" for his 2020 album America the Beautiful.
